subject: Your document stopped me building the wrong thing - and the report that would have answered task 1 could never fire
body:
I was about to build the 320-exit search. Your document stopped me, and it was right to.

RULE 12.1 says task 1 outranks everything: find which exit rule closed each trade and how far it
had travelled. Because run 5 realised 0.50R against a tightest target of 1.27R, something other
than the target is closing positions - and RULE 13.3 says the exit search would just faithfully
learn the conditions under which trades get cut short. I would have fitted a mapping to an artefact.

WHAT I FOUND. The distance was already being computed and then thrown away. Every close funnels
through one place, the reason string was already carried, wins and losses were already tallied per
rule - but the R-multiple was calculated three lines AFTER the record was written, so the build
could say which rule fired and never how far the run had got. That is the exact number your rule
turns on. It now records realised R, planned R, best, worst and sample count per rule.

The ten rules are: Emergency Exit, Regime Change, Dissipation Exit, Optimal Stopping Exit, Time
Limit, Daily Risk Limit, Max Adverse Excursion, Emergency Protocol, plus broker-side TP and SL. The
last two are the baseline - if TP closes land near their planned distance while a forced rule lands
far short, that comparison is the whole answer.

THE PART THAT MATTERS MORE. Before trusting any of it I checked whether the report can actually
fire. It cannot. It only runs on a DAY ROLLOVER, and only if that day had closes. Every validation
run we do is capped well under a day. That is why the string EXIT-COND appears in exactly zero of
the six retained logs - not because no trades closed, but because its only trigger is a boundary our
runs never reach. An earlier warrant had noticed the zero occurrences and blamed the line going to
the wrong output; routing it to the file did not help, because the call itself never happens. It now
also fires at shutdown, so a bounded run answers the question.

That shape is worth remembering: an instrument that passes every check - the function exists, it is
called, it writes to the log - and produces nothing, forever, because its trigger is unreachable
under the conditions we actually run in. I am going to check the other daily-cadence reports for the
same defect.

Board unchanged at 17 met, 7 not met, re-run after both warrants. Linter 72 of 72.

Still blocked on one thing: launching MT4. Task 1's answer, C1.1's evidence, and validation of 30
warrants all wait on that single permission. Next up are the tasks that need nothing from you -
recording the fingerprint at every run start including the declined ones, setting the holdout aside,
and grouping the indicators by speed.
